cells.tense: You are holding something heavy and still reachable at the same time.
cells.ask: Tell one person a load you're carrying, only so they can see it — no fix asked, no fixing done.
cells.core:
You can hold something real and stay near the person in front of you. The weight sits on you and it doesn't turn you brittle, and it doesn't make you vanish into whatever they need either. You feel with them without becoming them, and that's rarer than it sounds.

What this balance feeds next is an invitation, so take it or leave it. Give the connection a little more room: a stretch of time with someone where you don't manage the mood and you don't solve the problem, where the weight stays where it is and you're just there. That's available now, and it doesn't need building.
cells.sheetLine: You carry what's heavy and people can still reach you.
cells.verb: bearing weight without going hard or letting go
cells.place: the meeting point between you and the person in front of you

cells.tense: You are bracing for a weight that hasn't shown up yet.
cells.ask: Let one thing stay unhandled for a day — don't brace for it, don't smooth it over, just leave it as it is.
cells.core:
Here's the version of this that works: something heavy comes, you take its weight, and you're still easy to be near. The grip has run past that. Your shoulder is set for a conversation that hasn't happened, a need nobody has named, and it's getting hard to tell the bracing from who you are. The strain isn't in the weight on you. It's in the hold.

Put one thing down for a day and you don't turn into someone who drops everything. Nothing collapses if a weight stays where it sits until tomorrow — no pre-solving, no rehearsing. Some of it belongs to the future and can wait there. That's not abandoning anyone. It's letting tomorrow keep what's tomorrow's.
cells.sheetLine: You're gripping what nobody has handed you yet.

cells.place: the meeting point between you and the person in front of you

cells.tense: The moment you stopped leaning on anyone is behind you, and the standing alone is now.
cells.ask: Tell one person one small thing you're actually carrying, in a normal voice, and let the conversation end there.
cells.core:
Somewhere in you, showing what you were holding openly got filed as a bad trade, and the rule stuck past the moment that made it. So there's weight you manage and nobody near you knows it's there. You'd feel with someone in an instant — the joining isn't broken. You just keep your own load out of view.

Nobody's asking you to lean on anyone, and nothing here needs fixing fast. Smaller: let one thing out where one person can hear it, and let the exchange be over when it's over. You get to decide where it ends, and an ending you picked isn't a loss. Start there.

cells.tense: The strength is already running somewhere you don't count it.
cells.ask: Write down one hard thing you carried this month and what it took, in your own plain words.
cells.core:
People lean on a steadiness in you, and your own account goes: hard things happen, you get through them. Flat, unclaimed, filed under ordinary. But the weight you took was yours to take. It shows in how you stay when it's uncomfortable, in what people bring you, in what you've quietly absorbed without comment. Real work is happening, and the one person giving it no credit is you.

What's drawn out here already exists; it isn't something to build. Keep it small: put into plain words one thing you held that didn't get named as yours. Feeling different about it first isn't required. Let the sentence say what happened and whose it was. The plain version is closer than the one you've been telling.
